questions.question: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was signed between the Indian National Congress and the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Muslim League.

The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak) and the All India Muslim League (led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah).

  • The pact accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
  • It also demanded Dominion status for India.
  • This session also reunited the Moderates and Extremists of Congress.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of India's independence (1947)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is J.B. Kripalani (Acharya Kripalani).

  • J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Indian National Congress during the transfer of power in 1947.
  • He was the husband of Sucheta Kripalani, the first woman Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.
  • The first session of independent India was held under his presidency.

questions.question: The only session of the Indian National Congress presided over by Mahatma Gandhi was held at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Belgaum (1924).

  • Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session of INC in 1924 (39th session).
  • This was the only session where Gandhi served as the President of the Indian National Congress.
  • The session focused on the Non-Cooperation Movement and the aftermath of the Chauri Chaura incident.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1885.

  • The Indian National Congress was founded on December 28, 1885.
  • Founder: Allan Octavian Hume (a retired British civil servant).
  • First session was held in Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College) with 72 delegates and presided by W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.question: The President of the Indian National Congress at the time of the Quit India Movement (1942) was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

  • Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the President of INC during the Quit India Movement (1940-1945).
  • He was the youngest Congress President (35 years old in 1923).
  • He served as India's first Education Minister after independence.

questions.question: The famous 'Vande Mataram' slogan was first sung at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress held at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

  • 'Vande Mataram' was first sung by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 Calcutta session of INC.
  • President of the 1896 Calcutta session was Rahimtullah M. Sayani.
  • The song was taken from Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel 'Anand Math' (1882).

questions.question: The Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at the Surat session in 1907. Who was the President of that session?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rash Behari Ghosh.

  • The Surat session (1907) was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh.
  • The split occurred over the election of the President and the Swadeshi movement.
  • The Moderates wanted Rash Behari Ghosh as President; Extremists wanted Lajpat Rai or Tilak.

questions.question: The Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress (1920) is significant because:
questions.option_2: Constitutional changes were made to allow mass participation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Constitutional changes were made to allow mass participation.

The Nagpur session of 1920 was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.

  • The INC's constitution was amended to allow mass participation.
  • The goal of 'Swaraj' (self-rule) was adopted.
  • The session also approved the Non-Cooperation Movement (which was launched earlier in September 1920).

questions.question: Who was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Badruddin Tyabji.

  • Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President of INC, presiding over the Madras session in 1887.
  • He was also the third President of INC.
  • He was a barrister and a prominent leader from Bombay.

questions.question: The 'Drain of Wealth' theory was propounded by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

  • Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).
  • He argued that British rule was draining India's wealth to England.
  • He was known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'.

questions.question: The All India Forward Block was founded by ______ in 1939 after resigning from the Congress Presidentship
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

  • All India Forward Block was formed on May 3, 1939 in Makur Unnao, Uttar Pradesh.
  • Its formation was announced in Calcutta.
  • Bose resigned from the Congress Presidentship to form this party.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for the Covenanted Civil Service in 1863.
Reason (R): The Indian Services Act, 1861, passed during Lord Curzon's viceroyalty, reserved certain posts for covenanted civil servants.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

  • Assertion (A) is true: Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for the Covenanted Civil Service in 1863.
  • Reason (R) is false: The Indian Services Act, 1861 was enacted during Lord Canning's Viceroyalty, not Lord Curzon's.
  • Charles Cornwallis is known as the 'father of Civil services in India'.

questions.question: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded as a response to Muslim fundamentalism in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1915.

  • Hindu Mahasabha was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya.
  • The first All India Hindu Mahasabha Conference was held at Haridwar (1915).
  • In 1930, it emerged as a distinct party under Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.
  • Prominent leaders included Lala Lajpat Rai, Navin Chandra Rai, and Radha Mohan Das Agarwal.

questions.question: Who among the following said that 'English education has enslaved us'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

  • Mahatma Gandhi criticized English education for enslaving Indians.
  • Muhammad Iqbal wrote the famous song 'Saare jahan se achha' and gave the 'idea of Pakistan'.
  • Muhammad Ali Jinnah was the founder of Pakistan.
  • Raja Ram Mohan Roy is known as the 'Father of Modern India' or 'Father of the Bengal Renaissance'.

questions.question: In 1921-22, farmers of the Malabar seacoast of Kerala undertook a great uprising, which is known as the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Moplah uprising.

  • The Moplah uprising was led by Variyamkunnath Kunjahammed Hajj against the British and Hindu landlords.
  • The Wagon tragedy occurred when Moplah prisoners died of suffocation during transportation in a closed freight wagon.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers of British India is known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gopal Hari Deshmukh.

  • Gopal Hari Deshmukh was known as Lokhitwadi.
  • Balashtri Jambhekar is known as the Father of Marathi Journalism and started the first newspaper 'Darpan'.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is William Jones.

  • The Asiatic Society was founded in 1784 in Calcutta by Sir William Jones.
  • It was started with the goal of promoting oriental studies.
  • Jonathan Duncan started Sanskrit College (1791) at Varanasi to study Hindu Law and Philosophy.

questions.question: The Social Service League was founded in Bombay by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Narayan Malhar Joshi.

  • Narayan Malhar Joshi founded the Social Service League in 1911.
  • He also started the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in 1920.
  • He was the first general secretary of AITUC.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the time of India's Independence in 1947, the literacy rate was about 20 percent.
2. The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951.
3. Conduct of census in India is a Union subject under Article 246 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 only.

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The literacy rate in 1947 was about 12-16%, not 20%.
  • Statement 2 is correct: The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951.
  • Statement 3 is correct: Census is a Union subject under Article 246 (Seventh Schedule, Serial No. 69).

questions.question: What was the title given to the late Sarojini Naidu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nightingale of India (Bharat Kokila).

  • This title was given to Sarojini Naidu by Mahatma Gandhi.
  • Her notable works include 'The Golden Threshold' and 'The Broken Wing'.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots of 1875 took place in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

  • The Deccan Riots began at Supa village (Poona) in 1875.
  • Farmers destroyed account books of moneylenders and socially boycotted them.
  • The movement was supported by the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (co-founded by M.G. Ranade).

questions.question: Editor of a Marathi newspaper 'Kesari' was
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

  • 'Kesari' was a Marathi newspaper started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1881.
  • He also started 'Mahratta' (English newspaper).
  • Through these newspapers, he spread nationalist ideas and criticized British rule.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Bengal in 1770:
1. In 1770, Bengal and Bihar faced a massive earthquake that destroyed most villages.
2. The British government spent 50,000 on rebuilding houses for the affected population.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Neither 1 nor 2.

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The year 1770 saw the Bengal Famine, not an earthquake.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The British spent about 15,000 on importing food grains, not 50,000 on rebuilding houses.

questions.question: Tribal leader Birsa was associated with which tribe?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Munda.

  • Birsa Munda was a tribal reformer, religious leader, and freedom fighter from the Munda tribe.
  • November 15 is celebrated as Birsa Munda's birth anniversary.
  • Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on November 15, 2000.

questions.question: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was associated with which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahar.

  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was born into the Mahar community, which is listed as a Scheduled Caste in India.
  • He was the chief architect (Father) of the Indian Constitution.
